odoo.task: find-user (find one user among 100,000; p16 contacts not built, so the critic used the largest list, users from the shared dataset)
odoo.notes: Harness verdict: loss, because keystrokes tie at 21 (a tie is a loss). Ours wins steps, machine seconds and human seconds. Ours path: click Users > type the name > Enter, which opens the single result. Odoo's best per metric: Ctrl+K > /users > Enter > name > Enter > click, or Apps > Settings > Manage Users > name > Enter > click. Both products must type the full name plus Enter, so ours cannot win keystrokes until quick search ranks by relevance (for example 'yousef wang' + Enter opening the best match) or opens on fewer typed keys. The critic wrote the task and both drivers (compare-drivers/). Three runs per product, all verified. find-record (contacts) is not compared because p16 does not exist.

biggest_gap.title: The isolation gate cannot see a cross-tenant leak through the list engine unless a tenant B marker appears in the response
biggest_gap.detail: Every list registered with p05 relies on G1 to catch leaks automatically, but G1 only flags a leak when one of tenant B's id or text markers shows up in a response. A shared cache in the list engine that carries tenant B's aggregates (totals, group counts, sums) into tenant A's answers passes every gate. The process-state gate also exempts the list bindings: ModuleCatalog._modules is reviewed wholesale, so instance fields of ListBinding<T> are never inspected. Grouping with totals is exactly where money modules will cache. The gate needs to (a) inspect ListBinding and other per-registration objects for mutable state, and (b) check list totals and group counts that tenant A receives against tenant A's own row count (for example, compare the first-page total with an exhaustive keyset walk, and the group counts with A-only database counts, after B ran the same queries). A second, smaller gate gap is G2: it never checks shared-view PUT/DELETE by a user who holds lists.views.share but not the list's permission.
biggest_gap.evidence: Apply gauntlet/evidence/p05-list-search/r1/plants/L3-engine-count-cache.patch (a ConcurrentDictionary of totals keyed by search|filter in ListBinding.QueryAsync). Run `dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~Erp.Gates.Tests.G1`: everything passes (run-L3P1P2.log). Live on a stack with the plant: gulfsteel GET /api/identity/users?search=a → total 1004; then alnoor, same query → total 1004; alnoor with an uncached key → total 2005 (plant-live-demo.txt). For G2, apply P2-delete-without-list-permission.patch and run the G2 filter: 17/17 pass, while a lists.views.share-only user deletes the users list's Team view with 204.

other_findings: Keyboard defect: the column header buttons (sort 'Name', 'Options for the column E-mail' and the others) live inside the grid's onKeyDown. Enter on them opens the active record instead of sorting or opening the column menu, and Space does nothing. Sort and filter from headers is therefore mouse-only, against the keyboard-first rule (07-enter-on-column-options-opens-record.jpg; scripts/hdr.mjs: Tab to the button, press Enter, and the URL gains &open=<row id>).

Columns do not line up. With the default columns at 1440 px, rows with long e-mails shift the E-mail, Language, Status and Last sign-in cells right by up to 37 px, because each row's grid template sizes itself (01-users-list-en.jpg; email-cell x per row 543,543,543,543,551,566,543,...).

Bulk actions: the only built-in bulk action is Copy, and no screen registers a data-changing one. Ctrl+A selects only the loaded rows; there is no 'select all N that match' for acting on 100,000 rows, which Odoo offers.

Filters from headers are one condition per column, joined with AND. The engine supports or/not (checked through the API: '(language eq ar or isActive eq false) and not displayName startsWith M' → 29,504 in 41 ms), but the screens cannot build an OR.
Picking a record in the Ctrl+K palette only filters the users list (?q=email). A second Enter is needed to open it.

Arabic search does not normalise spelling variants: 'فاطمة' finds the user but 'فاطمه' does not; 'الزعابي' finds it but 'الزعابى' does not. For UAE data this is a chance to beat Odoo that is not taken.

Quick search ranks nothing: results keep the default sort (-createdAt). 'yousef wang' returns 46 rows with the wanted user anywhere. Relevance ranking (trigram similarity) plus Enter-opens-top-hit would cut keystrokes below Odoo's on find-one-among-100,000.

Performance is good. Over 100,004 users, round-trip medians are 8-42 ms for exact, partial, email and filter searches; 58 ms for search 'a' (all rows); 103 ms for 'Wa'; 182 ms for skip=99,000. Keyset walks over 7 sort orders (nullable lastSignInAt included) returned every row exactly once (api-timings.txt).

Positive: a list registers through ModuleBuilder.List with a typed filter language and its errors localised. Trigram GIN on display_name/email_normalized and (tenant_id, column, id) btree indexes exist. Saved views (personal/shared/default) persist across reloads, the viewer cannot share (no checkbox; API 403), and saved views are audited with actor and old/new values.

English and Arabic: the users list is fully RTL with Arabic chrome, plural counts are right ('100,005 مستخدمين'), and Enter-opens-single-result works in Arabic (08, 09). The only Latin text in the chrome is a user-named view.

[route: p03-identity] While testing the keyboard, three stray keys on the users screen (n, g, Enter) created a real user 'G' <g@alnoor.example> with no confirmation. The 'n' hotkey opens New user, and Enter submits a one-letter entry with an invented address. A guard or confirmation for a derived e-mail would prevent accidental accounts.

[route: p00-foundation] The G1 process-state gate allow-lists ModuleCatalog._modules wholesale ('list registrations with their query bindings… never tenant data'). Any mutable state hung off a module registration (list bindings, menus, future report or export registrations) is therefore invisible to the inspector. It should descend into registration objects rather than trusting the reason.

The comparison harness at this commit has no users-list task. The critic added tasks/find-user.mjs with ours and odoo drivers (kept in compare-drivers/). The Odoo keyboard path needs a wait for the palette input before typing '/users'.
